anchors.paper_title: Alljoined-1.6M: A Million-Trial EEG-Image Dataset for Evaluating Affordable Brain-Computer Interfaces
anchors.reason: The paper's title, authors, 20 participants, 1.6M trials and 32-channel consumer EEG match the dataset README's own reference, so it is this dataset's data paper.

metadata.methods_description: Participants viewed images for 100 ms followed by 100 ms of blank screen in an RSVP paradigm, with an orthogonal oddball detection task (button press on Woody character catch trials). EEG was recorded at 256 Hz with 32 Ag/AgCl gel electrodes in an extended 10-20 montage centered on occipital and visual regions. Each session had 19 blocks of about 5 minutes. Data were exported as EDF and converted to BIDS with MNE-BIDS.

citation_details.title: Seeing Like a Brain: Predicting Subject-Specific EEG Responses to Natural Visual Stimuli
citation_details.author: Hanchuan Peng, Jiaqi Yang, Baodan Bai
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Predicting how natural visual stimuli evoke individualized neural dynamics is a fundamental challenge in cognitive neuroscience and brain–computer interfacing. Here, we present an open-source framework that directly predicts subject-specific, whole-head electroencephalography (EEG) responses from natural images. The model combines a visual encoder, EEG decoder and multi-scale dilated temporal refinement to generate 63-channel, time-resolved responses, with multi-objective training jointly constraining temporal, spectral and semantic consistency. Evaluation across 10 subjects and unseen test concepts demonstrates robust zero-shot prediction, with particularly strong fidelity over occipital regions. The predicted EEG preserves early visual components, spectral characteristics and image-related representational geometry while enabling millisecond-scale inference.
